verdict.rationale: Porkbun documents scoped API keys that can be restricted to specific domains and to source IPs/CIDRs, which covers scoped credentials and IP allowlisting directly. The 2FA leg is thin: the docs only mention in passing that account two-factor authentication exists, and one community user reports using a passkey, with no first-party detail on supported factors or enforcement. missing for 10: first-party documentation of the account 2FA methods (TOTP/WebAuthn/passkeys) and enforcement options, documentation of key permission scopes beyond domain restriction, independent hands-on corroboration of IP/domain key scoping.

support.subject: As a security engineer, the registrar account itself is defensible — real 2FA, scoped API credentials, and IP allowlisting on API access

citations.quote: each key can be limited to specific source IPs (CIDR supported) and/or specific domains from the gear icon next to the key. A leaked scoped key can only touch the domains you listed, from the network you expect.
Porkbun API keys work regardless of whether account two-factor authentication is enabled — you never have to weaken account security to automate.
I use them for all my domains, albeit with a passkey for my account.
